question: In Table 3, how much lower is the heat generation of the ZrO2 loading with the least heat than that of the bare material, and how much higher is its onset temperature?
rendered:
- [other] Table 3 Onset temperature and heat generation for bare and ZrO2 coated Li1.2 Ni0.16Mn0.56Co0.08 O2 (NMC) materials.
- [result] The ZrO2 coated NMC materials showed an increase in onset temper-ature and decrease in heat generation with coating thickness when com-pared to bare materials.
- [result] The heat generation in 2 wt. % ZrO2 -NMC mate-rial, however, was high which may be due to different extent of reaction of slightly different amount of sample loading.
- [result] The ZrO2 coated NMC materials show improved cycling performance, as shown in Fig. 4 B(f).
- [result] The bare NMC exhibited rapid capacity fade with cycling, whereas ZrO2 coated NMC materials show significantly improved capacity retention. 1.5 and 2.0 wt.% ZrO2 coated NMC show the best capacity retention of around 95% at 50 cycles.
- [result] Moreover, bare NMC also displayed fast volt-age decay with successive cycling when compared with ZrO2 coated NMC materials, as shown in Fig. 4 B(g-h).
- [result] The heat generation for bare NMC material is 666.42 J/g.
- [result] The heat generation for 1.0 wt. % ZrO2 coated NMC material is 487.31 J/g.
- [result] The heat generation for 1.5 wt. % ZrO2 coated NMC material is 446.25 J/g.
- [result] The heat generation for 2.0 wt. % ZrO2 coated NMC material is 688.96 J/g.
- [result] The onset temperature for bare NMC material is 231.93°C.
- [result] The onset temperature for 1.0 wt. % ZrO2 coated NMC material is 237.59°C.
- [result] The onset temperature for 1.5 wt. % ZrO2 coated NMC material is 245.31°C.
- [result] The onset temperature for 2.0 wt. % ZrO2 coated NMC material is 251.97°C.

The heat generation of the ZrO2 loading with the least heat (1.5 wt. %) is 446.25 J/g, which is 220.17 J/g lower than that of the bare material (666.42 J/g).
The onset temperature of the ZrO2 loading with the least heat (1.5 wt. %) is 245.31°C, which is 13.38°C higher than that of the bare material (231.93°C).
